Overview

This tutorial accompanies selectFiberseqLociWorkflow 0.99.1 or later and follows the function-reference tutorial format: function tables, executable examples, plots, and result exports.

Leiden clustering and autocorrelation have separate sections below. Leiden groups reads by their m6A patterns. Autocorrelation describes repeating patterns within each read as a function of distance in base pairs. ACF profiles can also be clustered with their own independent Leiden analysis.

Analysis Input features Controls Result location
Manhattan-distance Leiden Observed m6A sites or bins clustering, window_size, k_neighbors, resolution, seed Locus colData$cluster and metadata$clustering
Autocorrelation All consecutive bases in the locus autocorrelation, max_lag Separate ACF experiment with lags in rows
Optional ACF clustering PCA of the ACF profiles ACF clustering, n_pcs, n_neighbors, resolution, seed ACF colData$acf_cluster and ACF metadata

The two top-level switches are independent. They use the same sample sheet. ACF settings do not change the m6A assay, read order or Manhattan cluster labels.

Functions used

Function What it does
make_sample_sheet() / prepare_regions() Define the shared inputs.
analyze_loci() Extract full-span reads; optionally run either analysis.
locus_autocorrelation() Compute ACF on an existing locus without rereading tracks.
autocorrelation_profile() Report means, SD, SEM and valid/invalid read counts.
plot_autocorrelation() Draw mean curves or a per-read heatmap.
write_autocorrelation_results() Export the ACF experiment, tables and PDFs.
write_locus_results() Export locus results and any attached ACF results.

Before you start

Install version 0.99.1 or later of the package following its README. The extra R packages uwot and irlba are needed only for ACF clustering. This tutorial uses them in the worked clustering examples. Python is not required.

install.packages(c("uwot", "irlba"))
library(selectFiberseqLociWorkflow)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(GenomicRanges)
stopifnot(packageVersion("selectFiberseqLociWorkflow") >= "0.99.1")
stopifnot(requireNamespace("uwot", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("irlba", quietly = TRUE))

Download the synthetic test

Download these two files into the same directory:

  • R Markdown tutorial
  • Synthetic test dataset (ZIP)

The ZIP contains two bgzip/tabix BED12 m6A tracks, their indexes, a relative-path sample sheet, a region table, ground-truth labels, checksums, and the complete R generator. This is entirely synthetic, freely reusable data (CC0-1.0), not an extract of the LCL samples. It contains 50 reads over a 2,000-bp artificial locus: 24 with planted 180-bp spacing, 24 with planted 220-bp spacing, and two zero-call controls. Both libraries contain both periodicities. This simplified model demonstrates ACF behavior; it is not a biological nucleosome simulation. The package’s existing example_data() contains real LCL tracks, so it is not used as the synthetic test here.

Knit with the default run_lcl: false anywhere the package is installed. The real example needs access to the project’s saved LCL input and report files:

# Synthetic example only: no LCL files required.
rmarkdown::render("autocorrelation-tutorial.Rmd")

# Include the real LCL analysis on the project filesystem.
rmarkdown::render("autocorrelation-tutorial.Rmd",
    params = list(run_lcl = TRUE, project = "/project/spott/cshan/fiber-seq"))

synthetic_zip can point to a ZIP elsewhere. Set output_dir to a new or empty folder to retain exports; the default uses a temporary directory. To select another existing LCL run, edit lcl_run and lcl_region in the YAML header. The values used to produce this page are recorded here:

knitr::kable(data.frame(setting = c("package_version", "run_lcl", "lcl_region"),
    value = c(as.character(packageVersion("selectFiberseqLociWorkflow")),
              params$run_lcl, params$lcl_region)))
setting value
package_version 0.99.1
run_lcl TRUE
lcl_region rank01_rs12470189_chr2_119290945_119291178 
run_dir <- if (is.null(params$output_dir)) tempfile("acf-tutorial-results-") else
    path.expand(params$output_dir)
if (file.exists(run_dir) && (!dir.exists(run_dir) ||
    length(list.files(run_dir, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE))))
    stop("Choose a new or empty output_dir")
dir.create(run_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

Prepare the shared synthetic inputs

Unzip and verify the files

The archive keeps paths relative to samples.tsv, so the download is portable. The code extracts to a new temporary directory each time it runs.

stopifnot(file.exists(params$synthetic_zip))
data_dir <- tempfile("acf-synthetic-input-")
dir.create(data_dir)
unzip(params$synthetic_zip, exdir = data_dir)
data_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "synthetic-autocorrelation")
checksums <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "checksums.tsv"))
stopifnot(identical(unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(data_dir, checksums$file))),
                    checksums$md5))
samples <- make_sample_sheet(file.path(data_dir, "samples.tsv"))
regions <- prepare_regions(read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "regions.tsv")),
    coordinate_system = "bed")
validate_inputs(samples, regions)
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(samples)[, c("sample_name", "sample_label", "m6a_format")])
sample_name sample_label m6a_format
synthetic_A Synthetic A bed12_fibertools
synthetic_B Synthetic B bed12_fibertools 
regions
#> GRanges object with 1 range and 2 metadata columns:
#>                             seqnames    ranges strand |             region_id
#>                                <Rle> <IRanges>  <Rle> |           <character>
#>   synthetic_periodicity chrSynthetic 1001-3000      * | synthetic_periodicity
#>                               tss
#>                         <numeric>
#>   synthetic_periodicity        NA
#>   -------
#>   seqinfo: 1 sequence from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths

The synthetic BED interval [1000, 3000) becomes chrSynthetic:1001-3000 in one-based inclusive coordinates. Every retained read spans the whole locus. Zero-call reads remain in the assay. No footprint tracks are supplied.

Leiden clustering

Fit Manhattan-distance Leiden on the synthetic reads

This section uses only the existing m6A clustering path. The settings here are separate from the ACF settings in the next section.

leiden_results <- analyze_loci(samples, regions,
    clustering = TRUE, autocorrelation = FALSE,
    window_size = 0, k_neighbors = 10, resolution = 1, seed = 1)
x_leiden <- leiden_results[[1]]
metadata(x_leiden)$clustering_status
#> [1] "complete"
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(sample = colData(x_leiden)$sample_label,
    cluster = colData(x_leiden)$cluster)))
sample cluster Freq
Synthetic A cluster1 6
Synthetic B cluster1 8
Synthetic A cluster2 6
Synthetic B cluster2 4
Synthetic A cluster3 4
Synthetic B cluster3 4
Synthetic A cluster4 3
Synthetic B cluster4 3
Synthetic A cluster5 3
Synthetic B cluster5 3
Synthetic A cluster6 3
Synthetic B cluster6 3 
ComplexHeatmap::draw(plot_locus(x_leiden, "heatmap", clustered = TRUE))

plot_locus(x_leiden, "profile", clustered = TRUE)

Manhattan clustering compares calls at corresponding genomic positions. Different periodicities and shifts can influence these clusters. The planted periods are not labels supplied to the fitting algorithm, and they do not require a particular number of Manhattan clusters.

Autocorrelation

locus_autocorrelation() — compute per-read ACFs

Compute ACF on the exact locus already used above. No input files are reread. max_lag = 500 returns 501 features: lag zero through lag 500. Lag zero is one for a nonconstant read. Curves omit lag zero by default so other lags are easier to see. Constant reads have undefined (NA) ACF values.

a <- locus_autocorrelation(x_leiden, max_lag = 500)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(a), colnames(x_leiden)),
          identical(colData(a)$cluster, colData(x_leiden)$cluster))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(status = colData(a)$acf_status)))
status Freq
constant 2
valid 48 
head(rowData(a))
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 1 column
#>         lag_bp
#>      <integer>
#> lag0         0
#> lag1         1
#> lag2         2
#> lag3         3
#> lag4         4
#> lag5         5

For a mean-centered binary read, ACF at lag k is the sum of products between bases k apart, divided by the fixed lag-zero sum of squares. The package uses stats::acf() with no smoothing and no lag-dependent overlap correction. All consecutive bases enter the calculation, including positions without calls.

autocorrelation_profile() — summarize valid reads

profile <- autocorrelation_profile(a, group_by = "sample")
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(profile[profile$lag_bp %in% c(0, 180, 220), ]), digits = 4)
lag_bp group mean_acf sd_acf sem_acf n_reads n_valid n_invalid
0 synthetic_A 1.0000 0.0000 0.0000 25 24 1
180 synthetic_A 0.1444 0.1809 0.0369 25 24 1
220 synthetic_A 0.1344 0.1855 0.0379 25 24 1
0 synthetic_B 1.0000 0.0000 0.0000 25 24 1
180 synthetic_B 0.1480 0.1876 0.0383 25 24 1
220 synthetic_B 0.1438 0.1881 0.0384 25 24 1 
stopifnot(sum(colData(a)$acf_valid) == 48L,
          sum(!colData(a)$acf_valid) == 2L)

Means exclude constant reads; n_reads, n_valid and n_invalid make that exclusion visible. SD and SEM are NA with fewer than two valid reads. Both samples contain both periodicities, so their mean curves should be similar.

plot_autocorrelation() — curves and heatmap

plot_autocorrelation(a, group_by = "sample", lag_range = c(1, 500))

ComplexHeatmap::draw(plot_autocorrelation(a, "heatmap", group_by = "sample"))

Use group_by = "cluster" to summarize by the original Manhattan clusters; this reads existing labels without fitting another clustering model.

plot_autocorrelation(a, group_by = "cluster")

Optional clustering of ACF profiles

The ACF method uses centered, unscaled PCA; correlation-distance neighbors; a uwot fuzzy graph; and igraph Leiden clustering. UMAP coordinates are for display. The independent ACF labels are zero-based and stored in acf_cluster. The original cluster column retains the Manhattan labels.

set.seed(123)
rng_before <- .Random.seed
acf_clustered <- locus_autocorrelation(x_leiden, max_lag = 500,
    clustering = TRUE, n_pcs = 50, n_neighbors = 10, resolution = 0.4, seed = 0)
stopifnot(identical(rng_before, .Random.seed),
    identical(colData(acf_clustered)$cluster, colData(x_leiden)$cluster))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(status = colData(acf_clustered)$acf_cluster_status)))
status Freq
clustered 48
zero_variance 2 
plot_autocorrelation(acf_clustered, group_by = "acf_cluster")

Reads with constant ACFs or insufficient usable information keep explicit statuses. Unassigned reads are excluded from acf_cluster views but remain in all/sample summaries and exports. Fewer than four valid reads cannot form an ACF clustering fit.

Check against the planted synthetic truth

Truth is joined after analysis, using sample and original read IDs. It does not affect the ACFs or either clustering model. The strongest positive local ACF peak in the 140–250-bp band should track the planted spacing.

truth <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "truth.tsv"))
cd <- as.data.frame(colData(acf_clustered))
key <- function(sample, read) paste(sample, read, sep = "::")
ix <- match(key(cd$sample_name, cd$original_RID), key(truth$sample_name, truth$original_RID))
stopifnot(!anyNA(ix), identical(as.integer(Matrix::colSums(assay(x_leiden))),
    as.integer(truth$n_calls[ix])))
cd$truth <- truth$truth[ix]
cd$period_bp <- truth$period_bp[ix]
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(planted = cd$truth, acf_cluster = cd$acf_cluster)))
planted acf_cluster Freq
period_180 0
period_220 0
zero_call 2
period_180 0 24
period_220 0 0
zero_call 0 0
period_180 1 0
period_220 1 24
zero_call 1 0 
peak_summary <- aggregate(positive_local_peak_140_250_bp ~ truth,
    data = cd[!is.na(cd$period_bp), ], FUN = median)
knitr::kable(peak_summary, digits = 1)
truth positive_local_peak_140_250_bp
period_180 180
period_220 220 
stopifnot(all(abs(cd$positive_local_peak_140_250_bp[!is.na(cd$period_bp)] -
    cd$period_bp[!is.na(cd$period_bp)]) <= 10))

Peak detection requires the complete band and a neighboring lag beyond it: max_lag >= 251. A missing peak means no qualifying positive local maximum, not a repeat length of zero. Peak agreement is the synthetic numerical check; cluster identities can vary across dependency versions.

Run either analysis, both, or neither from the same sample sheet

# Neither
analyze_loci(samples, regions, clustering = FALSE, autocorrelation = FALSE)
# Manhattan Leiden only
analyze_loci(samples, regions, clustering = TRUE, autocorrelation = FALSE)
# ACF only
analyze_loci(samples, regions, clustering = FALSE, autocorrelation = TRUE)
# Both, with separate settings for ACF clustering
both <- analyze_loci(samples, regions, clustering = TRUE, autocorrelation = TRUE,
    autocorrelation_options = list(max_lag = 500, clustering = TRUE,
        n_pcs = 50, n_neighbors = 10, resolution = 0.4, seed = 0))
a <- metadata(both[[1]])$autocorrelation
metadata(both[[1]])$autocorrelation_status

A failed optional ACF computation warns and records a status while preserving the locus and Manhattan fit. Check autocorrelation_status before using the attached result. ACF graphs and metadata describe the original run; recompute with locus_autocorrelation(x_subset) after subsetting a locus.

Real LCL example: rs12470189

This example uses the rank-1 locus in the native R workflow under code/clustering_methods/auto_correlation. The saved default analysis is chr2:119290056–119292055, a 2,000-bp window centered using the workflow’s rule around rs12470189 at position 119291056. Its cached input contains 255 phased reads from 15 contributing libraries at the time this tutorial was prepared. The code below reports actual counts on every run.

Exact input selection and provenance

The LCL pipeline selects full-span reads with at least one m6A call and a phased focal heterozygous genotype (0|1 or 1|0, HP1/HP2). A standard package sample-sheet run retains all full-span reads, including zero-call and unphased reads. Consequently, using the same locus and samples alone does not reproduce the pipeline’s read selection.

To demonstrate the exact current analysis, we reuse its read-only m6a_input.rds cache and the accompanying selection signature. We convert only the container orientation (reads × bases to bases × reads), preserve its read order and phasing metadata, and recompute ACF with the package. We do not rerun phasing or alter any saved LCL results. The real input files are not part of the synthetic download. If the cache is missing, run your native R pipeline first.

Load the existing run and create its sample sheet

lcl_dir <- file.path(params$project, params$lcl_run)
selection_path <- file.path(lcl_dir, "inputs", "selection_signature.rds")
input_path <- file.path(lcl_dir, "inputs", params$lcl_region, "m6a_input.rds")
report_path <- file.path(lcl_dir, "outputs", params$lcl_region, "report_data.rds")
stopifnot(all(file.exists(c(selection_path, input_path, report_path))))
selection <- readRDS(selection_path)
input <- readRDS(input_path)
report <- readRDS(report_path)
r <- report$region
stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1L, identical(as.character(r$region_id), params$lcl_region),
    identical(rownames(input$binary), input$records$row_id),
    identical(input$records$row_id, report$row_ids),
    ncol(input$binary) == r$width,
    identical(as.integer(colnames(input$binary)), seq.int(r$analysis_start, r$analysis_end)))
cohort <- strsplit(r$contributing_samples, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
sm <- selection$sample_table[match(cohort, selection$sample_table$sample_name), ]
stopifnot(!anyNA(sm$sample_name), !anyDuplicated(sm$sample_name))
lcl_samples <- make_sample_sheet(data.frame(sample_name = sm$sample_name,
    sample_label = sub("_.*", "", sm$sample_name),
    m6a = file.path(sm$fire_dir, "extracted_results", "m6a_by_chr",
        paste0(sm$sample_name, ".ft_extracted_m6a.{chr}.bed.gz")),
    m6a_format = "bed12_fibertools"))
lcl_regions <- prepare_regions(data.frame(chr = r$chr,
    start = r$analysis_start - 1L, end = r$analysis_end, region_id = r$region_id),
    coordinate_system = "bed")
knitr::kable(data.frame(sample_name = cohort,
    retained_reads = as.integer(table(factor(input$records$sample_name, levels = cohort)))))

This sample sheet can be used with either analyze_loci() switch. For a new unfiltered extraction on the same samples and region, use the following call; it is not the phased-cache analysis used for the comparison below:

lcl_all_full_span <- analyze_loci(lcl_samples, lcl_regions,
    clustering = FALSE, autocorrelation = TRUE,
    autocorrelation_options = list(clustering = TRUE, n_pcs = 50,
        n_neighbors = 10, resolution = 0.4, seed = 0))

Convert the exact phased input to a locus experiment

records <- input$records
stopifnot(all(records$sample_name %in% lcl_samples$sample_name),
    all(records$haplotype %in% c("HP1", "HP2")),
    all(records$focal_genotype %in% c("0|1", "1|0")),
    all(records$allele_status == "phased_focal_genotype"))
cd_lcl <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(records, row.names = records$row_id)
cd_lcl$RID <- records$row_id  # unique sample + molecule key used by the package
cd_lcl$sample_label <- lcl_samples$sample_label[
    match(records$sample_name, lcl_samples$sample_name)]
positions <- seq.int(r$analysis_start, r$analysis_end)
m <- Matrix::Matrix(t(input$binary), sparse = TRUE)
dimnames(m) <- list(paste(r$chr, positions, sep = ":"), records$row_id)
rr <- GRanges(r$chr, IRanges::IRanges(positions, width = 1L))
names(rr) <- rownames(m)
x_lcl <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(m6a = m), rowRanges = rr,
    colData = cd_lcl, metadata = list(region = lcl_regions, samples = lcl_samples,
        input_source = input_path, input_md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(input_path))))
stopifnot(identical(unname(as.matrix(assay(x_lcl))), unname(t(input$binary))))
knitr::kable(data.frame(reads = ncol(x_lcl), bases = nrow(x_lcl),
    samples = length(unique(colData(x_lcl)$sample_name))))
reads bases samples
255 2000 15

Recompute native R ACF and independent ACF clusters

Use the saved run’s settings rather than assuming its defaults. For the current resolution04 run these are 2,000 lag features (0–1999), 50 requested PCs, 10 neighbors, resolution 0.4, and seed 0.

p <- report$params
knitr::kable(data.frame(parameter = c("n_features", "n_pcs", "n_neighbors", "resolution", "seed"),
    value = unlist(p[c("n_features", "n_pcs", "n_neighbors", "resolution", "seed")], use.names = FALSE)))
parameter value
n_features 2e+03
n_pcs 5e+01
n_neighbors 1e+01
resolution 4e-01
seed 0e+00 
lcl_acf <- locus_autocorrelation(x_lcl, max_lag = p$n_features - 1L,
    clustering = TRUE, n_pcs = p$n_pcs, n_neighbors = p$n_neighbors,
    resolution = p$resolution, seed = p$seed)
#> Warning in irlba::prcomp_irlba(values, n = pcs, center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE, : The `tol` truncation argument from `prcomp` is not supported by
#> `prcomp_irlba`. If specified, `tol` is passed to the `irlba` function to
#> control that algorithm's convergence tolerance. See `?prcomp_irlba` for help.
stopifnot(identical(dim(t(assay(lcl_acf))), dim(report$acf)),
    identical(unname(is.na(t(assay(lcl_acf)))), unname(is.na(report$acf))))
max_difference <- max(abs(t(assay(lcl_acf)) - report$acf), na.rm = TRUE)
stopifnot(max_difference < 1e-12)
knitr::kable(data.frame(check = "Maximum absolute ACF difference from saved native R run",
    value = max_difference))
check value
Maximum absolute ACF difference from saved native R run 0 
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(status = colData(lcl_acf)$acf_cluster_status)))
status Freq
clustered 255

This numerical comparison checks the same reads, base positions, lag count and normalization. Cluster labels can vary with dependency versions; the ACF method and package versions are recorded in metadata(lcl_acf)$autocorrelation$clustering. The tutorial does not reinterpret HP1/HP2 as REF/ALT: that requires the saved focal genotype and allele mapping. Existing allele labels remain in colData.

plot_autocorrelation(lcl_acf, group_by = "acf_cluster", lag_range = c(1, 500))

ComplexHeatmap::draw(plot_autocorrelation(lcl_acf, "heatmap",
    group_by = "acf_cluster", lag_range = c(1, 500)))

plot_autocorrelation(lcl_acf, group_by = "sample", lag_range = c(1, 500))

Export results

Save the synthetic analyses separately

write_locus_results() preserves the original Manhattan analysis. write_autocorrelation_results() saves the independent ACF experiment with both label columns. Output directories must be new or empty.

write_locus_results(leiden_results, file.path(run_dir, "synthetic-leiden"))
write_autocorrelation_results(acf_clustered, file.path(run_dir, "synthetic-autocorrelation"))
if (params$run_lcl)
    write_autocorrelation_results(lcl_acf, file.path(run_dir, "LCL-autocorrelation"))
knitr::kable(data.frame(file = list.files(file.path(run_dir, "synthetic-autocorrelation"))))

The ACF export contains autocorrelation.rds, reads.tsv, lags.tsv, mean/SD/SEM tables, profile/heatmap PDFs, and acf_edges.tsv when clustering was requested. For an analyze_loci(..., autocorrelation = TRUE) result, write_locus_results() exports its attached ACF automatically under each locus’s autocorrelation/ subdirectory. To reload a standalone ACF result:

restored_acf <- readRDS(file.path(run_dir, "synthetic-autocorrelation", "autocorrelation.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(assay(restored_acf), assay(acf_clustered)),
          identical(colData(restored_acf), colData(acf_clustered)))
